subject: Acme Analytics — sudden p95/p99 regressions tied to request queue buildup
summary: Customer-facing escalation: Acme reports elevated p95/p99 latency. Root cause traced to request queue depth and deferred batching on Hosted API during a traffic pattern change. Customer demands mitigation, timeline for fix, and potential credit. Execs looped for prioritization.
messages:
From: Dave Hart <dave.hart@acme-analytics.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@acme-analytics.com
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sharp p99 spike starting 09:00 PT — urgent

Soojin,

We started seeing a sharp p95/p99 spike in our production calls to Redwood's Hosted API around 09:00 PT. Error rate remains low but tail latency has doubled for the past two hours — many requests are timing out on our end at 10s. This is impacting our realtime scoring pipeline.

Attached a few request logs and a short CSV of timestamps. Can you confirm whether this is on your side and what the mitigation plan is? Our customers are seeing degraded UX.

Thanks,
Dave
Product Ops — Acme Analytics

Attachments: request-log-samples.txt, customer-quote-of-traffic.xlsx
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Dave Hart <dave.hart@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sharp p99 spike starting 09:00 PT — urgent

Dave — thank you for the quick flag and the logs. We're on it.

Quick summary for now: SRE is seeing increased queue depth on the hosted inference tier serving your model family starting ~08:50 PT; this manifests as higher p95/p99 when batch windowing increases under bursty input. Error rate remains low as you noted.

Immediate actions we're taking:
- Ethan's team will throttle batching window for the affected pool and enable aggressive KV cache hits for repeated prefixes.
- We'll provision a small burst slice (dedicated warm capacity) to cut tail latency while we assess root cause.
- Grace from CS will coordinate customer messaging and timelines.

Expect a follow-up within 30 minutes with telemetry and a temporary mitigation roll. If we need a longer window for a fix, we'll escalate to dedicated capacity options and a credits discussion.

— Soojin
Head of Customer Escalations
Redwood Inference
From: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Dave Hart <dave.hart@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 09:58:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sharp p99 spike starting 09:00 PT — urgent

On Mon, Sep 28, 2026 at 09:34, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> Dave — thank you for the quick flag and the logs. We're on it.

Status update:
- Root cause (preliminary): sudden shift in request size distribution from Acme's side (more many-short requests with high variance) caused the serving runtime's batching heuristic to expand windows to achieve amortized throughput. That increased queue depth and raised tail latency under your SLA target.
- Mitigation applied at 09:45 PT: reduced max batch window to 8ms for the affected pool and pinned kernel selection to lower-latency path for short sequences.
- Telemetry: p95 improved from ~420ms to ~180ms within 4 minutes after the change. p99 remains elevated (~620ms) but trending down. See attached Grafana snapshot.

Next steps (24 hours):
1) Keep the reduced batch window for 2 hours while monitoring p99. If stable, we'll roll a more conservative batching heuristic tuned to Acme's traffic pattern.
2) Add an adaptive short-seq fast path so future variance doesn't expand windows. ETA for rollout to hosted: 3 business days behind canary.
3) If volatility continues, propose a short-term reserved burst (1-week add-on) so queueing is eliminated during spikes.

I've opened INF-7821 to track the follow-up work.

Ethan
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: grafana-p95-p99-20260929.png
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Dave Hart <dave.hart@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 10:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sharp p99 spike starting 09:00 PT — urgent

Dave — thanks for bearing with us. A couple notes for your comms team and customers:
- We believe customer requests that hit repeated short-prefix patterns will benefit from the KV cache tweak we're enabling. That should reduce observed latency for repeated patterns significantly.
- We will keep you posted every 2 hours and provide a short post-incident note with root cause and mitigation steps.

Would you like Redwood to draft a short customer-facing note for your status page? If yes, we'll include timelines and recommended retry/backoff guidance.

— Grace
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Executive Team <execs@redwood.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Dave Hart <dave.hart@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Acme outage risk — request from sales: mitigation + compensation framing

Team — looping execs because Acme is a strategic PLG customer at pricing tier Plus-Enterprise and they're asking about credits if this impacts their revenue. Summary:
- Incident: radial increase in p95/p99 starting 09/28 tied to queue build at hosted inference pool for their model family.
- Impact: degraded real-time scoring for several enterprise customers of Acme during business hours.
- Action taken: SRE reduced batch window and enabled short-path kernels; telemetry shows p95 back near baseline, p99 improving.

Request: can we pre-approve a customer credit up to 10% of last 30-day invoice for a partial SLA miss if p99 stays elevated >48 hours, and budget for an emergency 1-week reserved burst for Acme if they opt in?

Reasoning: avoid churn and keep the account stable while we implement longer-term fixes (INF-7821).

— Marcus
Enterprise Account Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Dave Hart <dave.hart@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, legal@acme-analytics.com
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 17:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme Analytics — follow-up and next steps

Dave — finalizing the follow-up: thank you for the patience. Quick closing notes:
- Short-term: SRE kept conservative batch window; p95/p99 returned to acceptable ranges for most traffic shapes. We left the burst slice in place for 24 hours and removed it at 16:40 PT today after observing stable tail metrics.
- Mid-term (next 72 hours): INF-7821 work items: adaptive batching heuristic (canary 3 days), short-seq fast path rollout (5 business days), automated prefix-kv warming for repeated keys (7 business days).
- Compensation: Marcus has proposed a conditional credit up to 10% if p99 remains >600ms for more than 48 hours post-incident. Pricing/finance will confirm.
- Communication: Grace will send a customer-facing postmortem draft by EOD tomorrow.

We're committed to a high-quality serving experience; please let us know if Acme would prefer us to enable a longer reserved burst while we ship the mid-term changes.

Best,
Soojin
On Wed, 30 Sep 2026 at 17:06, Dave Hart <dave.hart@acme-analytics.com> wrote:
> Thanks — the quick interventions helped. We'll discuss internal SLAs tomorrow and get back on the burst option. Appreciate the transparent updates.
>
> — Dave
